hints: Compare the energy at Y with resistance to the energy at Y if none of the gravitational energy decrease is dissipated.
walkthrough: With the 76 N resistive force, the kinetic energy at Y is 300 J.
With no resistive force, the full 3200 J decrease in gravitational potential energy becomes kinetic energy at Y.
The ratio is 300/3200 = 0.09375, which rounds to 0.094.

hints: For the same child, kinetic energy is proportional to the square of speed.
Take the square root of the kinetic-energy ratio 0.094 to obtain the speed ratio.
walkthrough: For a fixed mass, E_K = ½mv² means E_K is proportional to v².
Therefore (v_with resistance / v_without resistance)² = 0.094.
Taking the square root gives v_with resistance / v_without resistance = √0.094 = 0.31.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses E_K = ½mv², or equivalently E_K ∝ v² for the same child.
Takes the square root of 0.094 to obtain a speed ratio of 0.31.

hints: First account for the gravitational energy decrease that does not appear as the child's kinetic energy at Y.
That missing energy is work done against the 76 N resistive force; use W = Fs to find the slide length.
walkthrough: The child loses 3200 J of gravitational potential energy but has only 300 J of kinetic energy at Y.
The remaining energy is transferred by work against resistance: W = 3200 − 300 = 2900 J.
For the average resistive force, W = Fs, so s = W/F = 2900/76 = 38.2 m.
The length of the slide is 38 m to two significant figures.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds that 2900 J is transferred by work against the resistive force from 3200 J minus 300 J.

hints: At maximum compression, use the spring's elastic potential energy and its spring constant.
Set 140 J equal to ½kx² with k = 63 N m⁻¹, then solve for x.
walkthrough: For a spring within the proportional region, E_P = ½kx².
At maximum compression, 140 = ½(63)x².

ai_rubric.observable: Uses E_P = ½kx², or the equivalent ½Fx with F = kx, for the compressed spring.
Obtains a maximum compression of 2.1 m.

hints: Identify the elastic potential energy stored in the spring as the useful output and the child's kinetic energy as the input.
Calculate percentage efficiency as (useful output energy / input energy) × 100.
walkthrough: The useful output is 140 J of elastic potential energy in the spring.
The input is the child's 300 J kinetic energy at Y.
Percentage efficiency = (140/300) × 100 = 46.7...%, which rounds to 47%.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates percentage efficiency as (140/300) × 100 and obtains 47%.

hints: Relate the spring's elastic potential energy to its compression x while the spring constant remains fixed.
The relationship is E_P = ½kx², so consider how the graph gradient changes as x increases.
walkthrough: For this Hooke's-law spring, E_P = ½kx².
At x = 0 the elastic potential energy is zero, so the graph begins at the origin.
Because E_P is proportional to x², the energy rises more rapidly as compression increases: its gradient increases with x.
Sketch a concave-up curve from the origin to x = x₀, becoming progressively steeper.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a curved elastic-potential-energy line beginning at the origin.
Draws the curve with an increasing gradient as compression approaches x₀.
